programs.program: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (Sound / Ton)
programs.durationEcts: Programme page states 6 semesters / 120 LP (ECTS). The 6-semester figure is unusual for a 120-LP master — confirm with the programme office.
programs.language: German (DSH-1 German certificate is a hard admission condition)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Four core domains: audio engineering, sound mixing, acoustics/signal processing, and music. Students plan and deliver cinema sound mixes and act as sound supervisors on real film productions, building an individual 'sound language' through interdisciplinary artistic projects. Heavy Pro Tools use (the entrance exam itself is a Pro Tools scoring task). Strong industry pipeline into Babelsberg Studios.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed B.F.A. in Sound, a Tonmeister degree, or a comparable subject-specific degree; uni-assist evaluation for foreign qualifications; German at DSH-1 minimum; medical certificate of normal hearing plus an audiogram, both issued within the last year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The page requires a "completed Bachelor of Fine Arts in Sound, Tonmeister, or comparable subject-specific degree". A software-engineering BSc is not a comparable subject-specific degree, and no alternative talent route is offered.
programs.portfolioSpec: Documentation of works from the past three years, max 12 pages (PDF). Video compilation of at least THREE films on which the applicant did the sound design, 15 minutes total (MPG/MPEG/MP4/MOV/WMV, max 3.5 GB). At least ONE piece of music recorded or mixed by the applicant (WAV/MP3/MP4, max 5 GB). Tabular CV describing musical development.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site three-part aptitude test: (1) music test — intervals, harmonies, piano audition, critical listening/audio evaluation; (2) interview — presentation of submitted work plus subject knowledge; (3) practical exam — scoring a scene in Pro Tools.
programs.applicationOpens: 12 April (per the programme's own application page)
programs.deadline: 18 May 2027 for the winter-semester 2027/28 intake, as published on the application page. Verify directly — the page may still be showing an earlier cycle.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (Brandenburg public institution). Only a semester contribution/administrative fee; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (open to Tunisian graduates; funding usually starts 1 October); Deutschlandstipendium
programs.stipend: DAAD graduate scholarship pays a monthly stipend plus travel allowance and health insurance; exact 2027 monthly rate UNVERIFIED. The university itself pays nothing.
programs.facilities: Germany's oldest film school (founded 1954) on the historic Babelsberg Studios site, 30 min from Berlin. Cinema mixing stages, Dolby-standard theatrical mixing, full film-sound post chain. Reported acceptance rate 3–5% (secondary source, UNVERIFIED).
programs.fitNotes: Best-in-class for film sound in Europe, but effectively closed to him: it demands a prior sound/Tonmeister degree, DSH-1 German, an audiogram, and a portfolio of three finished films he has already mixed. Also the wrong target anyway — it trains film sound supervisors, not DJs/producers.

programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED (one aggregator lists 1 year; the ETI pages do not state duration or ECTS)
programs.whatYouStudy: Artistic recording direction (Musikregie): responsibility for the artistic result and quality of a music production. Combines musical-communicative competence with technical foundations and extensive hands-on practice in the ETI recording studios; work in broadcasting, film and TV, opera houses and theatres. Sister programme Musikübertragung (B.Mus.) is the bachelor-level Tonmeister track; a Music Acoustics M.Sc./Dr.-Ing. also sits at the ETI.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in Music Recording (Musikübertragung) or a Tonmeister diploma; proof of German; proof of health insurance; successful aptitude test.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The requirement is explicitly a "Bachelor's degree in Music Recording respectively diploma in Tonmeister". A music-specific/Tonmeister degree is required; no talent-based exception is published.
programs.portfolioSpec: Tabular CV; written statement explaining the choice of programme and intended study focus; a CD/DVD containing THREE productions made by the applicant within the past year.
programs.auditionSpec: Aptitude test: presentation of the three submitted productions plus a colloquium of approx. 30 minutes covering musical repertoire, technical principles and studio experience. Assessed by at least two committee members as 'qualified' / 'not qualified'.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: winter semester 15 February–15 March; summer semester 1 October–1 November (as published, no year stated).
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW public). Semester fee only; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists/All Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: The Erich-Thienhaus-Institut is the internationally leading German Tonmeister school; multiple recording studios and control rooms, strong links to broadcasters, opera houses and labels. Detailed console/immersive-room specs are in a scanned brochure that could not be reliably read — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The gold standard for classical recording engineering in Germany, and completely out of reach for him: it requires a Tonmeister bachelor plus three of his own studio productions from the last 12 months, in German. Also classical-recording-oriented, not electronic/club music. List it as a long-term aspiration, not a 2027 application.

programs.program: Popular Music M.A. – specialisation Producing / Composing Artist
programs.institutionType: Public university of popular music (state Hochschule)
programs.language: German (B2 required of international applicants by the end of the first semester)
programs.whatYouStudy: Two-stage structure: year 1 taught courses, year 2 an independent master project. The Producing/Composing track covers songwriting, arrangement, recording, sound design, beat programming, mixing, mastering, electronic music production, film music, game music, vocal producing and music-business practice — plus working as a production service provider for band projects. Facilities include professional recording studios (Tonstudio), the SMIX.LAB and a media library. Germany's only state Hochschule dedicated to popular music.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed first degree with a standard duration of at least 6 semesters; advanced practical musical experience; department-specific entrance examination; German B2 for international applicants by the end of the first semester.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check. The published requirement is only "a completed undergraduate degree with a minimum standard study duration of 6 semesters" — no subject restriction is stated, so his BSc Software Engineering satisfies the formal condition. Admission is decided almost entirely by the practical entrance exam, which does demand advanced musical ability.
programs.portfolioSpec: Upload of own musical productions; for performing/educating artists at least one live video (max 200 MB). Additional accepted material: videos, press coverage, photographs, cover artwork, scores, lyrics, teaching concepts. Exact number of tracks required for Producing/Composing is not specified on the application page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Live entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung), format varies by department. Typically 2–3 pieces performed, often the applicant's own compositions, with up to three accompanying musicians or playback; plus theory examination, improvisation test and interview.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (portal typically opens in the winter preceding the deadline)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 30 April (23:59 UTC upload deadline) for the following winter semester.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition for a first degree at the Popakademie itself, BUT Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG charges non-EU/EEA international students €1,500 per semester (≈€6,000 over 4 semesters). As a Tunisian national he falls under this fee.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (Tunisia eligible); Deutschlandstipendium. No Popakademie-specific scholarship found.
programs.facilities: Professional recording studios, SMIX.LAB, mediathek; faculty of working industry producers; located in Mannheim's Musikpark start-up cluster with dense German music-industry links.
programs.fitNotes: The single closest match in Germany to "I want to be a producer": actual beat programming, electronic production, mixing and mastering, taught by industry practitioners. Two obstacles: German B2 and a genuinely demanding live entrance exam, plus €1,500/semester as a non-EU student. He should treat this as his main German target and spend 2026–27 building a producer audition set and German.

programs.program: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium – postgraduate diploma at master level)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters plus 1 diploma semester (5 semesters total); ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1 concentrates on production/location sound; year 2 on post-production. Covers original sound recording on set, sound design, dialogue editing, mixing technique, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and Dolby Atmos. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students score the academy's own film productions.
programs.entryRequirements: Postgraduate (Aufbaustudium) structure implies a completed prior degree; Hochschulreife plus, where held, officially certified Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master must be submitted. No music degree is demanded.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — most likely yes. It is a Diplomaufbaustudium with no stated subject restriction and no explicit prohibition on non-music backgrounds; the filter is the practical entrance exam, not the bachelor subject. Confirm in writing before applying.
programs.portfolioSpec: Own projects/work samples uploaded via the online portal. Video work samples: max 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s. Exact number and duration of required audio samples not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Pre-selection on the file, then an on-site entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung) conducted in Pro Tools. Applicants must bring working knowledge of recording, sound design, mixing and bouncing.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (online portal typically opens in the autumn)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February.
programs.tuitionIntl: €0 for EU citizens; €1,500 for non-EU citizens per the programme page (whether this is per semester under the BW LHGebG or a one-off is not clarified on the page — confirm).
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand); Deutschlandstipendium. No academy-specific scholarship found.
programs.facilities: State-of-the-art audio post-production studios and current-industry on-set equipment, Dolby Atmos mixing, Foley stage; part of one of Europe's most production-active film schools with heavy German TV/film industry placement.
programs.fitNotes: The most realistic German film-sound route for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test rather than a conservatory audition, and the fee is low. But it makes film/game sound designers, not DJs. Worth applying only if he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing.

programs.program: Zeitabhängige Medien / Sound – Vision (sub-programme of Sound–Vision–Games)
programs.university: HAW Hamburg – Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften, Dept. Medientechnik
programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters (90 ECTS per aggregator; the HAW page states 3 semesters, ECTS UNVERIFIED on the official page)
programs.language: German (C1 required); English B1 also tested at interview
programs.focus: Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering; Live/Event audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-centred study at the intersection of science, technology and creative design. Modules cover audio technology and sound design, video technology and image design, VFX production, interactive design, lighting technology and design, plus production and project management. Eight required/elective modules in the chosen branch. Graduates go into audio/video/lighting manufacturers, production studios and theatres. Nationally unique in linking sound, moving image and games.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree with at least 210 ECTS in media technology, media systems, computer science, IT (applied IT or media specialism welcome), communication design, illustration or a related subject; German C1; English B1; passed aptitude test.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. The accepted-degree list names "computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome)". Caveat: it requires 210 ECTS, and many 3-year BSc degrees are 180 ECTS — he must check his SMU MedTech credit total.
programs.portfolioSpec: Between 3 and 10 work samples that "demonstrate your interest in and your aptitude and potential for your chosen branch" in detail and comprehensively. Accepted types: video, animation, light design, light installation, sound design, soundscape, music production, installation, performance, interactive/multimedia work.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage aptitude assessment: (1) portfolio/work-sample review; (2) interview if stage 1 is passed, at which German C1 and English B1 are verified. No instrumental audition.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: aptitude-test registration 1–31 October (one source says 'until 14 October'); formal application for the study place 1 December–15 January; entry SUMMER semester only, starting early April.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition. Semester contribution €397, including the semester ticket and the Germany-wide rail pass (Deutschlandticket).
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Art and Media Campus Finkenau, Hamburg: audio, video and lighting labs, studios for sound design and interactive media. Facility detail beyond the campus address is UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Structurally the friendliest German public option for a software-engineering graduate — CS degrees are named as welcome, the gate is a portfolio not an audition, and the total cost is €397 a semester. Two catches: German C1 (high), and the intake is April only, so a September 2027 start is impossible — he would target April 2027 (apply Oct 2026–Jan 2027) or April 2028. It is also more media/event technology than club-music production.

programs.institutionType: Public art university (music, theatre, dance, design)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic Composition; Sonic Arts
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-oriented master built around the student's own artistic development project. Four combinable specialisations: Electronic Composition, Instrumental Composition, Pop Composition, and Composition & Visualisation — students may mix them with different weightings. Teaching happens in the ICEM (Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien), which has trained electroacoustic composers since 1971 and shaped the current Integrative Komposition degrees.
programs.entryRequirements: A first university degree on which the master builds, OR proof of outstanding artistic talent; artistic aptitude established through the Eignungsprüfung; German B1 at enrolment; €50 application fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, in practice. The page states applicants need "a first university degree which the Master study course is based on" and separately allows entry on "proof of outstanding artistic talent"; the programme welcomes non-music backgrounds provided artistic aptitude is proven. The portfolio, not the degree subject, decides.
programs.portfolioSpec: Stage-1 digital submission of own works "in the form of original scores (especially for instrumental composition), recordings, videos etc." PLUS a concept/project plan for an artistic development project describing the intended master-thesis topic. Formats PDF and MP4, max 100 MB total. No fixed number of works is stated.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage Eignungsprüfung. Stage 1: digital preliminary round — portfolio and master-project draft assessed for technical/artistic ability and feasibility. Stage 2: in-person main round — approx. 30-minute colloquium on the submitted works, any revisions, artistic development and engagement with current artistic trends.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 March for the following winter semester; 15 November for the following summer semester.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). €50 application fee plus the semester social contribution (Studierendenwerk + NRW semester ticket); amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music strand), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: ICEM — one of Germany's oldest and most respected computer-music/electronic-media institutes (studio for live-electronic music since 1971), with a historic technical instrument collection; regular PACT Zollverein collaborations.
programs.fitNotes: A genuinely open door: no music degree strictly required, the decision rests on a portfolio plus a project concept, and it is tuition-free. But this is art-music electronic composition (electroacoustic, live electronics, installation), not dance-floor production — he would need to frame his work as compositional practice, and reach German B1.

programs.university: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic Composition
programs.whatYouStudy: Independent compositional work and professionalisation: mixed instrumental/electronic composition, installations and internet works, plus self-organised concerts of student-created music. The electronic and instrumental composition classes work closely together, so students can join the other class's projects and take main-subject lessons there. All practical work takes place in the Studio für Elektronische Musik.
programs.entryRequirements: "Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent"; an undergraduate degree in instrumental composition also qualifies; good computer skills (no prior electronics study needed); German A2 minimum; application via muvac.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Essentially No. The page states that "Bachelor graduates from other art or computer science fields" are admitted only "in exceptional cases of exceptional talent". Computer science is named — but as an exception route requiring exceptional demonstrated talent, not a normal pathway.
programs.portfolioSpec: Own works must be submitted for evaluation and are presented and discussed at the colloquium. The specific number, duration and format of works is not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (submission runs through the muvac platform).
programs.auditionSpec: Qualifying examination consisting of a colloquium: presentation and discussion of the submitted works, with questions on the applicant's own musical aesthetics and prior knowledge of contemporary music. No instrumental audition mentioned.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published on the programme page; applications run through muvac. Confirm with the Studio für Elektronische Musik.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester social contribution only; amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music); Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Studio für Elektronische Musik with several fixed and mobile workstations, comprehensive software/hardware and "excellent listening facilities"; Cologne is the historic home of the legendary WDR Studio for Electronic Music (Stockhausen).
programs.fitNotes: Prestigious and free, and the German bar is unusually low (A2). But the entry wording is the problem: without a composition bachelor he lands in the "exceptional talent" exception, which is a very high evidentiary bar for someone with no prior music training. Also purely art-music, no production/DJ content.

programs.university: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT Hamburg)
programs.language: English (the entrance examination is conducted in English). German B2 reported as required of international applicants by a secondary source — confirm with the Hochschule.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Sonic Arts; Immersive/Interactive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary programme for composers, media artists and computer scientists with musical interests. Fields: algorithmic composition, live electronics, game-engine development, video and light programming, digital recording, interactive installations, microtonal composition. Software explicitly taught: Max/MSP/Jitter, Ableton Live, Unreal Engine, MadMapper, TouchDesigner, Lightkey. Access to an AV Media Center and a digital recording studio.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree in music, composition, media art OR computer science; submission of artistic works; passed entrance examination. Language requirement: examination in English; German B2 reported for international applicants (secondary source).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — best fit in Germany on this criterion. The programme is described as "aimed at applicants with a completed Bachelor's degree in music, composition, media art, or computer science" and is "designed for composers, media artists, and computer scientists with musical interests". A software-engineering BSc is squarely within scope.
programs.portfolioSpec: "At least three representative works which demonstrate the ability to artistically incorporate the use of digital media, especially in the field of computer music. These works can be in the form of scores, texts, recordings, computer programs, videos, etc. and/or interactive websites."
programs.auditionSpec: Two-part entrance examination: (1) a 3-hour written exam — interactive computer-music tasks, text analysis, and multiple-choice questions on digital-media terminology; (2) a 15-minute interview about the submitted work and the applicant's motivation. No instrumental audition.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — the programme page gives no deadline; applications are made online via the HfMT portal for the winter semester. Contact the department office.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (Hamburg public). Semester contribution only; amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (Music / All Disciplines), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: AV Media Center and digital recording studio; Hamburg's Musikhochschule sits in a city with a very strong electronic/club scene. Studio detail beyond this is UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest realistic German target for him alongside the Popakademie: a CS bachelor is explicitly welcome, the portfolio can include code and interactive work as well as tracks, the entrance test rewards technical ability over conservatory ear-training, and instruction is in English. Caveat: it is computer music / installation / live electronics, not commercial dance production — he must be genuinely interested in Max/MSP and algorithmic work, and should confirm the German requirement.

programs.program: Künstlerische Musikproduktion (Artistic Music Production) – Master of Music
programs.university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years); ECTS not stated on the page — UNVERIFIED
programs.whatYouStudy: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands: (1) practical production work across genres and formats, exploring and applying the most recent production methods; (2) instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; (3) technical methodology and musical analysis, including acoustics and ear training. Aim is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; German B2 certificate or equivalent; successful completion of the concentration-specific proficiency test (Eignungsprüfung); €50 test fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — formally plausible, practically hard. The page requires a bachelor's degree without naming a subject, so a non-music degree is not excluded on paper. However the proficiency test includes an instrumental/vocal audition and written tests of musical and technical hearing, which presuppose real conservatory-level musicianship.
programs.portfolioSpec: Work samples submitted in advance and evaluated by the committee. The exact number, length and format of the required work samples is not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (check the Eignungsprüfungsordnung / Anforderungen page).
programs.auditionSpec: "The proficiency test involves the evaluation of work samples to be submitted in advance as well as completion of an instrumental/vocal audition. In addition, there is a practical task in the intended major as well as written examinations of musical and technical hearing ability." Test fee €50.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 1 March (date-of-receipt stamp of the university applies). Entry possible in winter or summer semester.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester contribution and €50 proficiency-test fee; contribution amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music); Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM) studios; RSH also runs the Ton und Bild engineering degree jointly with HS Düsseldorf, so the audio/video infrastructure is substantial. Console/immersive-room detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Content-wise excellent — a real music-production master with a Jazz/Pop track. The killer is the entrance exam: an instrumental or vocal audition plus written musical and technical ear tests. Without conservatory training he would very likely fail this, and it is in German at B2. Realistic only after two-plus years of serious instrument and ear-training work.

programs.program: Klang und Realität (Sound and Reality) – Master of Music
programs.university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electronic Music / Live Electronics
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-driven master integrating performative, compositional and algorithmic forms of contemporary art. Own projects sit at the centre and are re-conceptualised across two years on the basis of critical, multi-perspectival peer feedback. Two focus areas: Epistemic Media (art as a method of enquiry — acoustic research, documentary film, algorithmic composition) and Transmedia Forms (performance, sound art, installation, digital media). Musical practice is explicitly not tied to instruments.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent; German B2; aptitude assessment based on a detailed project proposal. No numerus clausus.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. "Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments; it encompasses many approaches to art and research. Accordingly, the master's program is open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds." This is the clearest published welcome to a non-music graduate of any German programme found.
programs.portfolioSpec: A detailed project proposal demonstrating the applicant's interests, motivations and skills, submitted with the portfolio. Number/length of accompanying works not specified — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Portfolio- and proposal-based aptitude assessment (Eignungsprüfung). No traditional instrumental entrance exam is mentioned.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 31 October, once a year. SUMMER semester entry only — courses begin at the start of April.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester contribution plus €50 proficiency-test fee; contribution amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien studios and collaborative project spaces; detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Formally the easiest German conservatory master for him to enter — open to all disciplinary backgrounds, assessed on a project proposal, no audition, no tuition. But it is artistic-research and transmedia work, not production craft: he would leave with a conceptual sound-art practice, not DJ/producer chops. Also April-only intake, so September 2027 is not possible (target April 2027 or April 2028).

programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters part-time at 50% workload / 60 ECTS total (15 ECTS per semester)
programs.focus: Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Music Production (design-research framing)
programs.whatYouStudy: "Development of audio experiences at the intersections of music, sound, language, technology, design, user experience and design research." Students pursue an individual project across the whole degree, supported by design-research seminars, interdisciplinary collaborations and guest-expert workshops. Trossingen also launched a Music Design master profile focused on Artificial Intelligence in Music (from 2023).
programs.entryRequirements: Open to applicants from many fields and disciplines ("aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen"); no specific bachelor subject mandated. Motivation letter describing musical/design background plus evidence of publications or competition results.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The page states the programme welcomes entrants "aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen" and mandates no specific bachelor's degree — a software-engineering background is compatible, and a design/UX-audio framing plays to his CS strengths.
programs.portfolioSpec: Project concept comprising: a self-introduction video of max 2 minutes; a written description of max 3 pages; and up to SEVEN previous works with accompanying descriptions.
programs.auditionSpec: No on-site aptitude test — "Es gibt keine Aufnahmeprüfung in Präsenz." Selection includes a short video interview of approximately 15 minutes.
programs.deadline: 1 March – 1 April, for the winter-semester intake (page references a start in October 2026 — for an October 2027 start, confirm the new window).
programs.tuitionIntl: "Keine Studiengebühren für EU-Bürger:innen bei Erstmaster" (no tuition for EU citizens on a first master). As a non-EU national he falls under Baden-Württemberg's €1,500/semester LHGebG fee unless a part-time exemption applies — UNVERIFIED, confirm directly.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies; Deutschlandstipendium. Note: DAAD scholarships generally require full-time enrolment, which a 50% part-time master may not satisfy — check before relying on this.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio/console detail published on the programme page.
programs.fitNotes: Uniquely low-friction entry: no in-person audition, a video interview, and up to seven free-form works as portfolio — ideal for someone with a self-taught catalogue. But it is 50% part-time and only 60 ECTS, sits in a very small town, is taught in German, and is oriented to audio UX/design research rather than club music. Also a part-time degree complicates both DAAD funding and a German student visa.

programs.university: Catalyst – Institute for Creative Arts and Technology (degree validated by Plymouth Marjon University, UK)
programs.institutionType: Private specialist creative-arts institute (state-accredited HEI; formerly dBs Music Berlin)
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts), awarded by Plymouth Marjon University
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time; ECTS/UK credit total not published — UNVERIFIED
programs.focus: Music Production; Electronic Music; Immersive/Spatial Audio; Sonic Arts
programs.whatYouStudy: Five integrated modules — Imagine (research proposal), Contextualise, Investigate, Present, Synthesise (final substantial original work). Three concurrent year-long workshops: Creative Sound Practices (modular synthesis, spatial sound, creative coding, field recording, improvisation, sound installation), Contexts of Listening (musicology, sound studies, philosophy, critical theory), plus one-to-one and group supervision and guest-artist sessions. The page is blunt: "This is not a studio engineering degree, a vocational production course or a genre-based music programme. It is postgraduate artistic research."
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline at Honours level (e.g. UK 2:1). Non-standard entry available for applicants without formal qualifications who can show relevant professional or life experience. English at IELTS 6 (or B2 for EU applicants).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — likely yes. The programme accepts applicants "from a wide range of backgrounds" and does not exclude non-music or computer-science degrees; applicants with non-standard qualifications are invited to contact admissions. Selection turns on the project proposal and portfolio.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of work PLUS a detailed project proposal framed as practice-led artistic research, PLUS a sample of research/academic writing, plus personal and educational documentation. Number/duration of portfolio items not specified — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: None. Written/portfolio application with admissions review; no live audition or on-site test published.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling; priority deadline carries a €1,000 tuition discount
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: for the 2026 intake, visa-required applicants 30 April 2026, EU/visa-exempt 5 June 2026, late applications to 28 August 2026; course starts mid-September. Expect an equivalent 2027 pattern (visa applicants ~April 2027 for a September 2027 start) — confirm.
programs.tuitionIntl: Self-pay fallback. Full-time: €6,028 per semester × 2 semesters, or €11,693 per year with a 3% annual-payment discount. Part-time: €3,678 per semester × 4, or €7,134 per year. Plus enrolment fee €895 per study year (includes visa support). Fees appear uniform for EU and non-EU.
programs.fundingLevel: None (self-pay). BAföG and German/EU national schemes are cited but are not open to a first-time non-EU international student.
programs.scholarship: €1,000 early-application tuition discount; €500 discount for combining a Summer Short Course with the degree; a €2,000 total tuition reduction is advertised across MA programmes. No means- or merit-based scholarship for non-EU students found.
programs.facilities: Located in the Funkhaus, the former GDR broadcasting complex — one of the world's great studio buildings. Multiple studios, extensive modular-synthesis equipment, ambisonics/multichannel diffusion, the internationally unique Monom 4D multichannel composition system, and a bookable gear library. Ableton Certified Training centre. Berlin's electronic-music ecosystem is on the doorstep.
programs.fitNotes: Best environment on this list for a would-be electronic producer — Funkhaus, Berlin, English-taught, no audition, one year. Two serious caveats: it costs roughly €12,600 for the full-time year with no funding available to him, and the school explicitly says it is artistic research, not vocational production training. Label this the self-pay fallback; the Berlin network may nonetheless be worth more to a DJ career than any degree on this list.

programs.program: Audio Communication and Sonology (double degree with the Institute of Sonology, Royal Conservatoire The Hague)
programs.degree: Double degree: M.Sc. (TU Berlin) + M.Mus. (Royal Conservatoire The Hague)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (60 per year); year 1 in Berlin, year 2 in The Hague
programs.language: English plus German — English at IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 83 minimum, and German at TestDaF TDN 4 for the Berlin year (the underlying Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc. is taught mainly in German and requires C1 for admission with foreign qualifications)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Immersive/Spatial Audio; Electroacoustic Composition; Sonic Arts
programs.whatYouStudy: Signal processing, electroacoustics, room acoustics, music informatics and virtual acoustics on the Berlin side; composition, live electronics, sound art, algorithmic composition and field recording on the Sonology side. Year 1 requires 39 ECTS of mandatory modules plus 21 ECTS of electives from the Audio Communication and Technology programme. Built on a long-standing collaboration on electroacoustic music and sound spatialisation.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's, master's or equivalent degree in science, engineering, humanities, social sciences, artistic-scientific, business or legal fields; engineering-level mathematics (Analysis I, Linear Algebra); knowledge of a programming language or computer algebra system; English IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 83; German TDN 4 (C1 stated for the parent M.Sc.). Numerus clausus applies to the parent programme.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — a technical degree is in fact the expected background. The parent programme's requirement is "a bachelor's, master's or graduate degree in a science, engineering, humanities or social sciences" field, with demonstrated higher mathematics and programming. His BSc Software Engineering fits better here than at any conservatory.
programs.portfolioSpec: A research project proposal is required with the application. No music portfolio requirement is published for the TU Berlin side — UNVERIFIED whether the Sonology side requires a separate creative portfolio.
programs.auditionSpec: None published on the TU Berlin page; selection is document- and proposal-based. Confirm whether the Institute of Sonology runs its own admission interview for year 2.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February (as published for the current year). Programme starts in October.
programs.tuitionIntl: TU Berlin charges no tuition — only the compulsory semester fee (social contribution plus public-transport ticket). In year 2 the Royal Conservatoire's regular tuition fees apply (Dutch statutory non-EU rate — amount UNVERIFIED). Travel, accommodation and living costs are the student's own.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines (Tunisia eligible); Deutschlandstipendium; Erasmus+ mobility support for the Hague year — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: TU Berlin's Audio Communication group (electroacoustics, virtual acoustics, spatial audio labs) plus the Institute of Sonology in The Hague — one of the historic centres of electronic music, with major studio and spatialisation infrastructure.
programs.fitNotes: Intellectually the strongest technical-artistic hybrid available to a software engineer, and nearly free on the Berlin side. But it is engineering-heavy (Analysis I and Linear Algebra prerequisites, C1-level German for the parent programme) and produces spatial-audio researchers and electroacoustic composers, not DJs. Worth listing because his CS degree is an asset here rather than a liability. Note: the plain TU Berlin "Audio Communication and Technology" M.Sc. is the same entry route without the Sonology year.

programs.university: SAE Institute Germany (mandatory modules in Bochum; electives at all German SAE campuses incl. Berlin) — degree awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
programs.city: Bochum (electives across Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Munich, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Leipzig, Hannover, Nürnberg)
programs.institutionType: Private specialist audio/media academy in partnership with a public art university
programs.degree: M.A. (Master of Arts), awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
programs.focus: Music Production; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Sonic Arts (project-based, cross-media)
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-based artistic master spanning music, film, video art, installation, sound art, photography and game art. Core modules: artistic practice, project planning, narration, contract law, marketing, event management. Elective modules cover audio, video, multimedia and lighting, plus perceptual psychology, design, real-time systems and media history. Mandatory modules run as weekend blocks in Bochum, so part-time employment alongside is feasible. Delivered with Folkwang's ICEM (Institute for Computer Music and Electronic Media).
programs.entryRequirements: A professionally qualifying higher-education degree (berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss) with a minimum of 180 ECTS, plus demonstration of artistic aptitude.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The only degree condition published is a "berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" with at least 180 ECTS — no subject restriction. A software-engineering BSc qualifies formally; admission then rests on the artistic project proposal.
programs.portfolioSpec: A written artistic project proposal, plus previous creative work reviewed at the colloquium. Number/length of works not specified — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: No performance audition. Selection is by colloquium with SAE and Folkwang representatives, reviewing the project concept and the applicant's previous creative work.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published; intake is every October. Contact SAE Bochum admissions.
programs.tuitionIntl: Self-pay: €400 enrolment fee, then either 24 monthly instalments of €485 (≈€11,640) or 4 semester payments of €2,838 (€11,352). Total roughly €11,750–€12,040.
programs.scholarship: None found for non-EU students. The award is a Folkwang (state university) degree, so DAAD Study Scholarships may in principle be usable — UNVERIFIED for a private-provider delivery model; check with DAAD before relying on it.
programs.facilities: SAE's German campuses are equipped audio/studio facilities (SAE is one of the largest audio-education networks worldwide); elective modules can also be taken at Folkwang University and its ICEM computer-music institute. Specific console/room detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: A genuine accredited master (state Folkwang degree) with no audition and no subject restriction — the most accessible formal qualification on this list. Downsides: German-only, ~€12,000 self-pay, weekend-block format in Bochum rather than a music capital, and a broad cross-media rather than music-production focus. Reasonable insurance policy, not a first choice.

programs.university: Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, Faculty of Art and Design
programs.durationEcts: Standard 2 semesters for applicants holding a bachelor of at least 8 semesters / 240 ECTS; shorter bachelors require additional bridge semesters (so realistically 3–4 semesters for a 180-ECTS BSc)
programs.language: English-language curriculum with some modules taught in German (Interface Design offers a fully English programme). German A2 required; English C1 (TOEFL 95 / IELTS 7.0).
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electroacoustic Composition; Sound Design (radio/acoustic ecology)
programs.whatYouStudy: Project- and experimentation-driven MFA covering organisation and technology alongside creative, analytical and critical skills. Six professorships shape the sound side: Electroacoustic Composition, Experimental Radio, Acoustic Ecologies, Media Environments, Interface Design and Media Events — an unusually deep concentration of sound chairs in one art faculty. Applicants define a planned master topic in advance.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Media Art and Design or an equivalent first university degree recognised as professionally relevant; German A2; English C1 (TOEFL ≥95 or IELTS 7.0); passed aptitude test; motivation letter of about one A4 page setting out the desired study focus and planned master topic. Applications go through the Bauhaus.CampusPortal, NOT uni-assist.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check. The requirement is a BFA in Media Art and Design "or equivalent first university degree recognized as professionally relevant" — relevance is judged case by case on the portfolio, so a software-engineering BSc with a strong media-art portfolio is arguable but not guaranteed. The 240-ECTS expectation is a second hurdle.
programs.portfolioSpec: "Artistic portfolio, i.e. a compilation of own artistic/creative works" as a PDF of max 20 MB, plus links to hosted interactive or time-based works where applicable. Plus a ~1 page motivation letter naming the planned master topic. No fixed number of works.
programs.auditionSpec: Aptitude test, portfolio-based, with a possible personal interview. No live audition. Results announced 6–8 weeks after the deadline.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: applications close 31 March; enrolment deadline 30 September; winter-semester start only.
programs.tuitionIntl: "No, there are no tuition fees, however enrolled students must pay a semester contribution fee." Contribution amount UNVERIFIED. Thuringia charges no non-EU tuition.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Fine Art/Design/Film strand), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Bauhaus heritage institution; the Experimental Radio and Electroacoustic Composition chairs run their own studios and broadcast infrastructure. Specific equipment detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Rare combination: tuition-free, largely English-taught, portfolio-only admission, and a real cluster of sound professorships. But the English bar is high (IELTS 7.0 — well above the IELTS 6.0 most programmes ask), the 240-ECTS assumption may force bridge semesters, and the output is sound art/experimental radio rather than production. A credible second-tier target if he can hit IELTS 7.

programs.program: Mediale Künste (Media Arts) – Diplom 2, postgraduate (MFA-equivalent), with Klangkunst / Sound focus
programs.degree: Diplom 2 (postgraduate diploma; the KHM states it is internationally comparable to an M.F.A.)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (postgraduate track); ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED
programs.language: German (most instruction in German; A2 certificate at application, B2 at enrolment)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Sound Design; Electronic Music
programs.whatYouStudy: Free, project-based artistic study: students choose and combine their own artistic focal points, supervised across disciplines by professors and technical staff. Klangkunst (sound art) is one of the available specialisations, delivered through the KHM's Klanglabor — project-oriented practice combined with current sound discourse via seminars, lectures, practical exercises and work presentations. The centre of the degree is the student's individually developed artistic project.
programs.entryRequirements: General higher-education entrance qualification (Abitur-equivalent) plus a completed higher-education degree in a relevant area of study. Alternative route: entrance qualification plus at least two years of professional artistic/creative practice. German A2 at application, B2 (Goethe-Institut) at enrolment. For Diplom 2, an outline for a potential project must be produced.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — computer science is named as a relevant prior field. The accepted areas include "IT and engineering sciences" (German listing: "Informatik, Fotoingenieurwesen" among others alongside theatre/film/TV studies, literature, art and cultural studies, communication design, visual communication). His BSc Software Engineering is directly in scope.
programs.portfolioSpec: Samples of artistic/design work — "videos, films, photographs, computer graphics, animations, drawings, texts, compositions, and music videos". For Diplom 2 additionally an outline for a potential project, typically 2–3 pages of text or sketches with explanations.
programs.auditionSpec: No multi-stage examination. A commission evaluates the submitted work samples; artistic suitability as shown in the portfolio is the decisive selection criterion. (Shortlisted applicants are normally interviewed — UNVERIFIED.)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: application period runs from mid-October to January/February; winter-semester start only.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition. "Contributions of approx. 400 euros per semester" covering the NRW-wide semester ticket, student union fees and equipment insurance.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Fine Art/Film strand); Deutschlandstipendium; KHM runs its own scholarship/Schaukasten programme for enrolled students — details UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Klanglabor (sound laboratory) and the exMedia Sound area; full media-arts production infrastructure (film, video, computer graphics) in Cologne — Germany's media capital, with the WDR broadcaster and a strong electronic-music history.
programs.fitNotes: Quietly one of the best-fitting options: it explicitly accepts computer-science graduates, admission is decided on a portfolio plus a 2–3 page project outline with no audition, and it costs ~€400 a semester. The trade-offs are German B2 and an art-school framing — he would be making sound art in the Klanglabor rather than learning mixdowns. Good if he wants Cologne, credentials and freedom rather than production drills.

programs.program: Audiovisual Media Creation and Technology (Audiovisuelle Medien) – M.Sc., profile 3D-Audio and Music Technology
programs.degree: M.Sc. (some sources list M.Eng. for the German-language variant — confirm which title applies)
programs.focus: Immersive/Spatial Audio; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Music Technology
programs.whatYouStudy: Three profiles: 3D-Audio and Music Technology, Visual Media Creation, and Computer-Generated Imagery. The 3D-Audio and Music Technology profile addresses current questions in audio technology with an explicit focus on 3D audio and its application in sound design, radio drama (Hörspiel) and interactive audio installations, worked through with high practical relevance in modern studios. Research- and leadership-competence oriented.
programs.entryRequirements: An internationally recognised university degree, ideally with a media-technology and media-design competence profile; ideally 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals (mathematics, informatics) and 15 ECTS in media applications (design, sound). Proof of German required. Motivation letter (max 2 pages) and letters of recommendation can improve the application ranking by up to 0.5 grade points.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — leans yes on the technical side, no on the media side. The programme "builds on a bachelor's degree in media technology or design", and international applicants need "a recognized university degree with a media technology and media design-related profile". A software-engineering BSc covers the engineering/informatics half (15 ECTS in maths/informatics is easy) but he would need to evidence ~15 ECTS in media/design/sound applications, which his degree probably lacks.
programs.portfolioSpec: No artistic portfolio is required. Individual motivation letter of max 2 pages, plus optional letters of recommendation from universities or employers.
programs.auditionSpec: None. Document- and grade-based admission via the HdM application portal; no audition or on-site test published.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 July for the winter semester; 15 January for the summer semester. Note one source states winter-semester entry only — confirm.
programs.tuitionIntl: Baden-Württemberg LHGebG applies: €1,500 per semester for non-EU/EEA students (≈€4,500 over 3 semesters). No separate programme tuition.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Modern audio studios used for the 3D-audio work, plus a television studio and full AV production infrastructure. Specific immersive-room/console detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The best German fit for immersive/3D audio with a technical entry route and no audition — his CS background is an advantage and there is no artistic gatekeeping. Two problems: he probably cannot show the expected media/design ECTS, and it is German-taught in Baden-Württemberg (€1,500/semester). Also engineering-flavoured: 3D audio, Hörspiel and installations, not producing tracks.

programs.program: Sound Studies and Sonic Arts (M.A.) — DISCONTINUED, DO NOT APPLY
programs.university: Universität der Künste Berlin (UdK) – Berlin Career College / ZIW
programs.degree: M.A. (Master of Arts) — closed to new entrants
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Sound Design; Electronic Music
programs.whatYouStudy: Was an interdisciplinary part-time continuing-education master between music, visual arts and media art, combining creative practice with theoretical study of auditory art, culture, design and reception; linked to the UNI.K studio for electroacoustic composition, sound art and sound research. Aimed at practising sound artists and sound experts with at least one year of professional experience.
programs.entryRequirements: Formerly: a university degree plus at least one year of professional experience, or exceptional creative talent. Now moot.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Moot — the programme no longer admits anyone.
programs.deadline: CLOSED PERMANENTLY. The official ZIW page states: "Der Studiengang Sound Studies and Sonic Arts nimmt ab sofort deshalb keine neuen Studierenden mehr auf" (the programme is accepting no new students, effective immediately). Enrolled students may finish. Note: the English-language programme pages are still live and still read as if recruiting — this is the trap. UdK plans new continuing-education formats in future, so the sound area may reappear under a different name.
programs.tuitionIntl: Was tuition-driven (fee-paying) as a continuing-education master; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: UNI.K – Studio für elektroakustische Komposition, Klangkunst und Klangforschung (still operating at UdK for other programmes).
programs.fitNotes: Included as a warning, not a recommendation. This is the programme most often suggested to people in his position, and its English pages still look open — but the German ZIW page confirms it has stopped admitting students as part of a restructuring of all UdK continuing-education masters. He should not spend time on it; he should instead watch UdK for a successor format and consider UNI.K-adjacent options.
